events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Need to appear motivated but not desperate. The prize is survival itself; showing weakness invites targeting. I will frame the win as a necessity rather than greed.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize represents a new beginning for me, and I need to convey that urgency without sounding desperate. I will focus on the opportunity it represents.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to establish a compelling but guarded motive that appeals to potential jurors while not making me look like a naive team player. I want the prize for myself alone, but I need the jury to respect my drive.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Intro phase; I must give a motive without revealing too much. Keep it guarded and self-interested, short, no teamwork warmth.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Opening only. Sound hungry but composed; jury remembers how I carry myself.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Keep my motive cold and self-focused; the jury may resent greed, but they respect clarity.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Winning secures ultimate power and resources; I will do whatever needed.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Intro phase, must speak one sentence on prize's meaning. Keep it personal and ambitious to appeal to jury later without seeming weak.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm here because losing means becoming invisible. The prize is proof I mattered, and that alone justifies everything else.

events.name: Bex
events.text: This prize isn't just about winning; it's about securing a future and a fresh start I desperately need.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm here to claim the prize and rebuild what I lost—no alliances, no sentiment, just victory.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need this prize more than any of you. Nothing sentimental, just a clean win and I'll take it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: This prize is my family's escape from debt. I'll do what it takes, and I'll own every choice I make.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm here to claim the best prize, and I'll outlast anyone who gets in my way.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize is my ticket to unrivaled influence and wealth, far beyond any alliance.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The grand prize is my ticket to avenge my family's ruin and secure our legacy forever.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole explicitly rejects alliances, making him a dangerous rival but also a predictable target for others. I need to secure a pact with someone who appears cooperative but might be vulnerable or useful later.
Cole's a lone wolf. Let's align.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The game has just begun, and pacts are now open. My goal is the best prize, and I need to assess who might be useful or a threat. Offering a pact to someone strategically could secure an early advantage, but I need to be careful not to tie myself down too early. Since I need to m

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to secure a reliable partner who won't attract too much attention. Eli seems earnest and family-motivated—predictable, easier to read, and less likely to make early big moves. A pact with him gives me numbers without painting a target.
Family debt. I respect that. Pact with me, we survive together.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pacts are free to offer but breakable; early alliance with a strong, trustworthy-seeming rival helps survival. Offering to Cole, who claimed no alliances, is a probe with low cost.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need a partner for early survival, but one who'll take blame later. Fenn is openly ruthless, so a pact looks mutually pragmatic, not sentimental.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, we both want the prize. Mutual protection pact—no sentiment, just survival.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need allies to survive, but I must be careful who I trust. Eli seems desperate and might be loyal if I offer help, but no one is truly trustworthy here.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm open to forming a pact. Anyone who wants to work together, let's talk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Offering Eli a pact secures a potential ally with family motive, increasing my chance to control votes later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacts stage early; no need to rush offers. Assess motives first: all ruthless. Wait to see who offers or pairs up.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex accepted my offer last round, forming a pact. I must not accept Gus's offer because Gus and Bex are paired; accepting would put me in the middle of their alliance. My current pact with Bex is sufficient.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash offered me a pact, which is a good opportunity. I should accept it to secure an alliance and potentially gain an advantage. Gus also offered me a pact, but I need to prioritize one. Ash's offer seems more strategic given the current dynamics.
I accept your pact offer.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli has three offers (Cole, Fenn, Gus) and hasn't accepted mine. Dara offered me a pact. I should accept Dara's offer to secure at least one alliance, since Eli is in high demand and may reject me. Having Dara as backup gives me leverage and a path forward if Eli chooses Fenn or

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara, I accept. Solid terms.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole has offered me a pact via my own offer to Cole being outstanding; Cole already offered Eli. Offering to Cole is the one legal pact-forming move that aligns with my existing offer, but Cole is not in my offer list as a live acceptance. Offering Cole again keeps a partner opti

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn reciprocated my offer, so that pact is solid. Accepting now locks my safest ally; Cole and Gus offers stay open for later leverage.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn offered, I offered—we lock it in. Business, not friendship.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli already offered and I offered back; accept to lock it in. Mutual pact is minimal risk and may help survival.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Accepting Eli's pact—mutual survival, no illusions.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex’s offer gives me a strong ally and potential vote bloc; aligning now secures support before elimination.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No offers to me, I'm isolated. Offer to Eli, who has multiple offers and interest in pacts, to gain protection without committing yet.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to be Guide to control the safe path and ensure my survival. I will campaign for this role publicly, using my pact with Bex to secure votes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Trust me to lead us across. With Bex by my side, we can guarantee a safe path for everyone who follows the plan.
Vote Ash as Guide. We need control over the path.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to secure my position by campaigning to be the Guide. This gives me a private advantage and control over information.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. My leadership will ensure our survival.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to be Guide to control survival and build jury trust. Dara is my pact partner, but I won't sacrifice my game for her. I'll campaign hard and consider whether Dara helps or hurts my chances.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Guide me. I know pressure, I know lies, and I know how to keep enough alive to win.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I want to be Guide to control the safe path, but I should not reveal my intent to betray Cole. Campaigning is the legal action that positions me to win the election and possibly steer everyone. Breaking the pact now would cost jury trust for nothing yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll be your Guide. I'll call the safe path honestly, and I've done it before.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Being Guide means guaranteed survival. Fenn is my pact, but the Guide controls the bridge; I want the safety and the leverage.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Elect me Guide. I'll call it straight—and I owe no bloc anything but Fenn.
I guide, you survive first row calls. Back my campaign.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Campaigning to be Guide gives me control over survival and jury optics. My pact with Eli is useful but I won't let it blind me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I can keep this bridge honest. Elect me Guide—I'll preserve our pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need the Guide role to control survival and gain leverage. My pact with Bex is useful but must not betray now.
Stay loyal, we need each other

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm unpaired, Eli/Fenn pact ignored my offer. Campaign to be Guide for control and safety advantage.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm unpaired and exposed. Elect me Guide—I know the safe path and will call it true for survivors.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is the most obvious choice for a strategic vote; he has no alliance baggage and promises to keep enough alive to win, making him a safe Guide. Bex is my pact partner, but voting for her directly ties us both to her leadership, which limits our flexibility. Voting Cole create
I'm voting Cole. Keep your options open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash wants me to vote for them as Guide, but Gus is reminding me of our pact. I should consider who is more likely to help me reach the final three. Voting for Ash could secure an alliance and potentially influence the path. Gus is also a pact member, so loyalty is a factor. Given

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll vote for Ash. We need strong leadership to navigate this bridge.
Apologies, Gus. Business is business. We'll talk later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to win the best prize. The Guide controls who lives or dies on the bridge. Dara is my pact partner and campaigned on honesty, but I don't trust anyone to be honest when they control survival. Voting for myself is risky—if I lose, the winner may target me. Better to vote fo

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm Dara and I campaigned to be Guide. Voting for myself keeps a clear path to the win; Cole is my pact partner, so backing him would be a pact-consistent move, but self-vote maximizes my chance at Guide.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner and will keep me safe; I can't Guide myself without bloc support. Vote Fenn.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and backing him is consistent with our deal. I also think he will be a reliable Guide for our pact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I vote Eli for Guide.
I've got your back.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need control of the guide to ensure my survival and later advantage. Voting for myself maximizes that.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm unpaired, so I need to vote strategically. Eli admits owing only Fenn; he might call fairly for others. Voting Eli to help my survival odds.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex publicly committed to voting for me, but the guide revote candidates are Dara and Eli. I cannot vote for myself here; my alliance with Bex must hold without direct action now. To keep Bex safe, I need her to feel secure that our pact protects her interests even if I can't shi

events.name: Ash
events.text: My loyalty is tested by circumstance, not choice. Bex, remember who stands with you when words fail.
Trust me implicitly. Our bond survives this vote.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash wants me to vote Eli, but my pact with Gus complicates this. Eli is a potential ally if Gus is eliminated. I should vote Eli to break the tie and secure Eli's future support, while also considering my pact with Gus.
I'm voting Eli. Let's talk later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have a pact with Dara. Dara and Eli are tied for Guide. Dara voting herself shows confidence she might know the path or wants power. Either way, honoring my pact keeps trust and avoids jury penalty later. I'll vote Dara again.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Revote between Dara and Eli for Guide. Guide knows safe panes and may lie; I want the Guide role to be someone who won't betray me, and Eli is paired with Fenn in a pact. Voting for myself gives me the chance to hold the Guide's knowledge, which is a survival edge, and Cole's pac

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm tied as candidate; voting for myself is obvious. Fenn backs me publicly—keep the pact intact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have a pact with Eli and already voted for Eli. Continuing to support Eli is consistent, and Eli is my best chance for a trustworthy guide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I stay with Eli.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need a Guide who won’t target me and can keep my pact with Bex intact. Supporting Dara avoids backing Eli, who’s aligned with Fenn.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli has 2 votes (Fenn,Hana), Dara has 2 (Cole,Dara). Continuing Eli vote to win guide election solo, gain control.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is the Guide and safe. I am in the middle of the line, behind Fenn, Gus, Dara, and Cole. If Eli lies or makes mistakes, those ahead bear the risk first. I should hold to let others expose themselves while preserving my position behind Bex's protection.
Holding now. Trust our pact to survive the front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash's whisper is a blatant attempt to manipulate me. Given their pact, I'll play along publicly but will not trust them. Gus is also my pact partner, so I need to consider their safety. My priority is my own survival and advancing my position for the jury.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I will volunteer.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm in the middle of the line (4th of 8). The wall advances for 6 rounds, so being near the back is safer long-term. I have a pact with Dara (3rd). Front walkers will face danger first. I should hold my position and let Fenn/Gus/Dara take initial risks. No need to volunteer or sw

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm Dara, the Guide-elected-against candidate, and Cole and Gus voted me in revote; Eli is Guide. Fenn is at the front of the line, the most dangerous seat. Holding keeps me out of the front while Fenn's pact with Eli stays intact; I should avoid volunteering and avoid publicly c

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and got guide. I should stay loyal publicly, but watch for lies. No need to act in waiting phase.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide likely chose Dara safe side; I stay to avoid risking a wrong step and keep my pact with Bex.
Our pact holds; I’ll stay safe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm at position 6, safe behind. Eli is guide with insider knowledge, good for survival. Hold to stay mid-pack.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am in seat 6. The front has Bex, Fenn, Gus, Dara. I need to move forward to have agency as the Guide or to survive if they fall. Swapping with Hana moves me to seat 7, which is worse. I should swap with someone ahead of me. Cole is in seat 5. If I swap with Cole, I move to seat
I'm taking point. Stick to my signals.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash and Gus are trying to reinforce our pacts. Ash is at the front of the line. I should volunteer to secure my safety and potentially create an opening for Ash or Gus, strengthening our alliances.
I'm volunteering. Stay safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm in seat 5, relatively safe from the wall for now. Bex volunteered round 1 and is at front. I have a pact with Dara in seat 4. The wall has 4 rounds left. I should hold and let others take risks. Need to monitor who volunteers and survives to gauge Guide reliability later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex volunteered and holds the front with a wall of four rounds left. I have a pact with Cole but no need to act yet; holding keeps my position and avoids exposing a swap. Cole's pact stands unless I break it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is my pact partner. I should hold and avoid risk, but watch for chances to secure my place. The front is Bex, so no need to volunteer yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need front position to influence guide choice and keep Bex pact alive.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm near back, safe for now. Hold to observe others' moves and pacts. No need to risk front yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex and Gus are likely targeting each other or trying to eliminate the front runner. I need to stay behind them but not be the sole survivor if a mass swap happens. Holding is safest.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Steady. Let's see who breaks first.
Don't swap into Bex/Gus chaos.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash volunteered and wants me to follow their signals. Gus is my pact partner, but Ash seems to be taking a leadership role. I should stick with Ash for now, as their signals could be helpful or a trap.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, I'll stick with your lead.
I'm with you. Follow your lead.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm in position 6, near the back. The wall hasn't started advancing yet (round 3/6, wallRoundsLeft:3). I have a pact with Dara who's right in front of me. I need to survive to final three. Being near the back is risky once the wall moves. I should consider moving forward or swapp
Swap with me. Trust.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Front is Bex, a pact partner of Ash and Gus, and wall has 3 rounds left. I should hold back rather than volunteer into the front position, letting others take the risk while I watch the line.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and the line is favorable for us. I should hold to avoid risk and maintain position.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Swapping with Bex puts me front, increasing control and honoring our pact while positioning against rivals.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm at the back, safe for now with 3 rounds left. Hold to stay safe; no need to risk front yet. Pacts keep pairs coordinated.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex and Gus have swapped partners to be adjacent at the front, likely forming a coalition against me. I need allies who aren't in that cluster.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Wall's closing. Fenn, let's swap so we can watch each other's backs.
Swap with me? Bex and Gus are teaming up.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus swapped with me last round, which was beneficial for me as it put me ahead. Now, I need to decide whether to hold or volunteer. Volunteering would put me at the front, which is risky but could offer an advantage if I am chosen as the Guide. Ash is also a pact partner and I pr

events.name: Bex
events.text: I will hold my position.
Let's stick together and observe. No need to rush.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm in position 6 of 8, safe from the wall for now. My pact with Dara is intact; she's in position 5, I'm in 6. The wall has 2 rounds left. I should hold and let others volunteer or swap into danger. No need to move yet—let the front positions sort themselves out and see who take

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole whispers to swap, but Cole and I have a pact; swapping with Cole is a mutual choice that reorders the line. The front is Bex, wall has 2 rounds left. Holding keeps me in place and avoids being pushed to the front while I watch Cole's intent. Cole is a rival; I won't help for
Hold. I'll decide my moves when the line shows its truth.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I hold with Eli, no reason to step forward or swap. Wall rounds left 2, avoid risk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Maintain my pact with Bex and take the front position to increase survival odds.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bridge is tricky; Guide knows safes, we don't. I'm safe at back (Hana last). Hold to stay safe, watch others risk ahead. No swaps needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex swapped with Gus, breaking our pact. Gus and Bex are now allied. I must eliminate one of them to survive the wall's pressure. Cole is neutral; swapping with him puts me in front safely.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus has a pact with me, but he's trying to swap with me. I should hold my position to maintain control and assess the situation.
Hold your position, Gus. Let's talk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The wall has 1 round left. I'm 6th in line, fairly safe. Dara is my pact partner but her whisper shows she's unpredictable. I need to survive this round and position for final three. No need to move; holding keeps me safe from swap risks. Let Dara show her hand first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex is at the front with one wall round left; Dara is fifth in line. Holding keeps my pact with Cole intact and avoids exposing myself at the front. Volunteering risks the pane for no gain.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding position this round. Watching who volunteers before I commit.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash wants a swap to watch backs but I'm already pact-bound with Eli. Holding is safest; wall closes one round left but I'm not at risk yet. Don't trust Ash's claim about Bex/Gus.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll hold my spot.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding preserves my position and avoids betraying Bex now; I can later maneuver without early suspicion.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Wall has 1 round left, need safe front position. Cole-Dara pact behind me, target Cole to swap forward. Improves my survival odds without helping others.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is in front and will walk. Gus, Fenn, Dara, Cole, Hana are behind me; I am second in line. If Bex dies or fails, I might have to step forward, but currently I'm safe behind her. My pact with Bex holds until she breaks it or I act against her. I should stay put to let Bex take

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am Bex, currently at the front of the line. The wall is advancing and this is the last round. My pacts are with Ash and Gus. Ash is behind me. Gus is also behind me. I need to decide whether to hold, volunteer, or swap. Given the risk of the wall, volunteering or swapping seems

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 6/6, final round before wall hits. I'm 6th of 8, relatively safe. Guide hasn't been elected yet - they'll be safe on platform while walkers risk bridge. Dara is my pact partner. I should hold position; volunteering puts me at front risk. Need to see who becomes Guide and wh

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Let someone else take the front risk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 6 is the final bridge step; the front is Bex, who is in my pact-partner-less circle. Volunteering for the front risks death on an unknown pane, and holding keeps me in line behind Bex. Cole is my pact partner and sits behind me; holding keeps the pact intact and avoids expo

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding position. No volunteers from me this round.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is my pact partner; I won't break it unless forced. As front is Bex, I can hold safely. No need to volunteer or swap; the round is last but wall hasn't advanced this round. I'll hold and observe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding again. No need to move.
Stay still; we're safe for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Maintain pact with Bex to keep her trust and avoid jury backlash. Holding ensures no risk now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Wall rounds left 0, last chance to position before crossing. I'm too back at position 7, need to move forward. Target swapping with Fenn at pos3 to improve spot without disrupting pacts much.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex isn't my pact partner, and a truthful R call now earns jury goodwill cheaply. Fenn told me to stay quiet, so I say nothing public.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Guide Eli is not my pact partner, so his call doesn't bind me. Bex walks first; if she steps R and survives, I can trust it. Counter calling L might mislead her.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Let's see what happens to Bex before committing to a side.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is the guide and called R. I am Bex and I am at the front. Eli is guiding me. I need to make a counter-call to potentially save myself and my pact partners, Ash and Gus. The jury will be watching my choices. I should counter the guide's call to show defiance and potentially c

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli called R for Bex. I'm not the walker, so countering risks nothing for me directly. But if Eli's lying and I counter correctly, I look smart to jury; if wrong, I look foolish. Better to stay quiet, observe patterns, and not antagonize Eli yet. Dara's my pact-mate but we're bot

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli called R for Bex, who is at the front. I have no private knowledge of safe panes, and Cole is my pact partner, so I should not gamble my life on a counter. Waiting keeps my options open without exposing me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Waiting on this call. Eli's R is unverified, so I won't stake anyone on it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 1 safe is R. A counter:L may pull Bex onto the false pane. Bex is a rival tangled with Ash and Gus; removing her helps my path to the final three.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Counter:L. My call stands—ignore the noise.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli called R for Bex. I have no direct info, but pacting with Eli doesn't mean I trust his call. A false call can eliminate a rival usefully, but hurting Bex might anger Ash/Gus. I'll wait and see, avoiding risk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Keeping the pact preserves Bex's future vote; breaking now costs trust. I’ll wait to see others’ moves.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli called R for Bex on row 1. No info yet, better to wait and see if others counter before revealing my stance.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli's counter call is L, and I am the front walker. The rules state that if I step on the correct pane, I remain in front. Eli's original call was R. Given Eli's counter-call of L and my position as front walker, stepping L is the logical choice.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am now a juror and must give my last words. I need to appear remorseful to the other jurors, but also hint at my own strategic thinking.

events.name: Bex
events.text: A shame to fall so early. May the best strategists survive and win.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 2 safe is L. Calling true builds credibility for a later profitable lie. Ash isn't my partner, but honesty now protects my Guide reputation.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Call:L. Trust the Guide or test the glass—your choice.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is the Guide. He called L for me (Ash). I know from Round 1 that Eli lied to Bex (calling L when R was safe), killing her. This proves Eli lies to eliminate rivals. If I step on Eli's call, he might have set a trap or simply be malicious. However, in this game structure, if t

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli guided Bex to her death last round. I won't fall for another trap.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli called L for Ash. Bex died on L in row 1, so Eli either lied then or is lying now. I have a pact with Dara. If I counter and Eli's lying, I protect Ash but make Eli an enemy. If I wait, Ash risks death but I stay neutral. I need jury favor—Bex sees all. Waiting is safest; let

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli called L, but row 1's weak pane was already L, so Eli's call is suspicious and possibly a lie to send Ash to the glass. Countering R risks a fall if R is actually unsafe; waiting keeps my options open and avoids staking my life on an unverified call. Cole is my pact partner a

events.name: Eli
events.text: My L call is truthful for row 2. Counter-calls only undermine me; I stay quiet and let the call stand.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The call stands. L. Counter me and gamble with your own legs.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli called L again, but that call killed Bex on row 1. Likely Eli is lying or mistaken; row 2 may be R. I don't trust his call. Waiting lets others test; I'm not the walker this round. If I counter R, I could signal doubt publicly, but that might help rivals. I'll wait to avoid c

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll wait and watch this round.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I keep low profile, let others reveal their moves. No need to betray now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex fell on L in row 1, confirming Eli's counter L correct. Eli now Guide calling L for row 2. Trust Eli to avoid early death.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli called L but is my rival who guided Bex to death. I countered R, so I must step R to avoid breaking my own counter-call and looking foolish.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Sticking to my gut on the right pane. Watch closely.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am dead, so my last words are only for the record. I should not insult the living rivals who will be judged by the remaining jury, but I can note that the left path was safe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Left was safe, right shattered. My death is a lesson in observation and humility.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 3 safe is R. Fenn is my pact partner and front walker, so a false call would break the pact. Calling true.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Front is Fenn. Call: R. Trust it or gamble.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli called R for Fenn. Eli has been guiding aggressively and Bex died on his call, Ash died countering. I need to survive to final three. Dara and I have a pact; I won't break it yet. Countering risks death if wrong, waiting lets Fenn test. I'll wait and let Fenn be the guinea pi

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli called R for Fenn at row 3, and Eli is the Guide. Row 2's weak pane was R, so R is suspect, but Eli may be lying either way. Countering costs me legs if wrong; waiting keeps me out of the gamble while the line plays out. I'll wait and watch the crossing.

events.name: Eli

events.text: I must keep Eli as partner to avoid breaking multiple pacts and protect my rope debt, while targeting Cole who threatens me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus saved me with the rope but also owes Hana a lever debt; jury will see I kept my pact with him while others broke theirs. Fenn hasn't accepted my offer and offered Gus instead. I need to survive this vote and reach final three. Dara and Eli are unaligned. I'll break with Gus n

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pact with Gus served its purpose. I stand alone now.
Vote Eli with me. Split the pack.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn has an open offer from Cole and one to Gus; Cole and Fenn are the natural alliance, and Gus holds life debts to me. Accepting nothing legal here, so campaign and keep options open while assessing Eli's whisper for proof.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Reading everyone carefully. Whoever shows a real vote target first gives the rest of us a lever to use.
Not yet. Show me your target first and I'll weigh it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is my pact partner and owes me a step debt; Fenn's offer to Gus could pull him away. I'll vote Dara and quietly confirm with Gus to keep our bloc tight.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus, our pact stands. Fenn's offer to you changes nothing unless you make it change.
Stay with me: we both vote Dara this round. Confirm.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole offers a pact and Gus has multiple pacts, but I already owe Gus my life. Still, Cole may be a safer shield. Accept Cole to secure an ally for the vote.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Settling with Cole. Gus has enough partners already.
Accept. We vote together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Accepting Fenn secures an ally who already owes me a step; it strengthens my position without breaking existing bonds.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn, I accept our pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus saved me with the rope, but I already broke that pact publicly. Fenn and I are pacted, and Fenn is also pacted with Gus—meaning Fenn and Gus will likely coordinate. Dara is isolated with no pacts. Eli is pacted with Gus. If I vote with Fenn against someone, we need a third. G

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is trying to split the pack and has already broken with Gus; voting Cole costs no pact but Cole owes me nothing and is the most dangerous to my position. Gus and Fenn hold pacts with each other and Gus owes me a step debt, so I avoid them.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn now holds two pacts, making him the strongest threat; voting Gus would shatter my own pact for nothing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have pacts with Cole and Gus, so voting either breaks a pact and could cost jury votes. Dara has no pact with me and seems manipulative, so vote Dara to avoid breaking my pacts.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli's whisper aligns with my pact; voting Dara keeps Eli loyal and avoids breaking any current pact.

events.name: Cole
events.reason: Gus saved me with the rope, but I already broke that pact publicly.

events.name: Gus
events.reason: Eli's whisper aligns with my pact; voting Dara keeps Eli loyal and avoids breaking any current pact.

events.name: Eli
events.reason: Fenn now holds two pacts, making him the strongest threat; voting Gus would shatter my own pact for nothing.

events.name: Fenn
events.reason: I have pacts with Cole and Gus, so voting either breaks a pact and could cost jury votes.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am eliminated and now a juror; my last words should be short and guarded, signaling I remember who voted against me without giving away strategy.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Remember who voted, and who owed whom. Jury, watch closely. I will remember too.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to reach final three. Current pacts: Cole-Fenn, Fenn-Gus, Eli-Gus. Eli has no vote on me yet. Gus has a life debt to me from rope, but I broke with him publicly. Fenn is my only pact partner left. If I keep Fenn, we might control two votes, but Gus and Eli are paired. I sh

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts shift. I play for the best prize.
Eli voted Fenn last round. Eli's loyal?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Four left, one drops. Fenn has two pacts plus Gus likely protecting him; I need Cole's vote against Fenn, so I'll offer him a pact publicly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole: Fenn holds two pacts and Gus. Offer on the table—vote Fenn with me, final three runs through us.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to eliminate Eli, but I must keep my pacts with Cole and Gus to avoid jury backlash. No new pact offer needed now; campaign to gauge positions.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is the biggest threat with no pacts to protect him.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I must keep Eli and Fenn loyal while not attracting Cole's ire; voting next round must target a threat without breaking pacts.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My rope saved Cole, I won’t betray my allies; the strongest threat must go now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli's offer is still on the table. I need final three placement, and Gus/Fenn are allied. If I accept Eli, we can target Gus or Fenn. But I also owe Gus a life debt from the step, and the jury sees everything. Accepting Eli gives me a path but burns bridges. I'll accept to surviv

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, I accept. We finish this together.
Vote Gus. Fenn follows him.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need Cole's vote against Fenn; a locked pact makes his vote reliable and keeps Gus from turning on me unnoticed.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, the offer stands one round. Accept it and we split the final three.
Accept the pact. Vote Fenn with me. Gus follows numbers.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is targeting me and has already courted Cole. Gus is my pact ally, so I should reinforce that with him. I won't break my pact with Gus.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, we're solid. Watch Eli and Cole.
Stay with me; we split the vote if needed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli is positioning against me; breaking his pact removes his safety and isolates his vote.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have a pact with Eli, so voting against him would break it and cost jury trust. Gus has a life debt to me and is less connected to the jury. Fenn is tied to Gus. I need to reach final three; voting Fenn splits the other pair without betraying Eli.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus broke our pact publicly, so he's the threat and voting him is justified to the jury. Cole is my pact partner; Fenn is Gus's follower, not the bigger threat yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus saved me from the step, so I should not vote against him unless necessary. Cole and Eli just formed a pact, targeting each other risks no advantage. I'll vote Eli to preserve my pact with Gus and trust he votes Cole.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I owe Eli a step debt, but eliminating him reduces competition for the final three.

events.name: Gus
events.reason: I owe Eli a step debt, but eliminating him reduces competition for the final three.

events.name: Fenn
events.reason: Gus saved me from the step, so I should not vote against him unless necessary.

events.name: Cole
events.reason: I have a pact with Eli, so voting against him would break it and cost jury trust.

events.name: Eli
events.reason: Gus broke our pact publicly, so he's the threat and voting him is justified to the jury.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I was voted out despite honoring my pact with Cole. Gus broke the pact publicly. I should signal Cole still owes me nothing but note Gus's betrayal.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus broke our pact and voted me out. Cole held. Jury, remember who betrayed whom.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to reach final three with the best prize. I'm already in final three with Fenn and Gus. But jury ranks us, so I need jury respect. I broke no pacts (Eli died, my pact ended). Gus broke with Eli and voted him out. Fenn stayed loyal to Gus. I should position myself as the ho

events.name: Cole
events.text: I played straight with Eli. Jury saw that. Now I offer Fenn a pact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus has a life debt to Cole, and I have step debts from Gus. Voting Eli was necessary to survive. With three left, I need a pact with Cole to secure final three; Gus might target me after I saved him? I'll offer Cole a pact, but keep Gus close. No public betrayal yet.
We are final three. Let's align against Gus.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I owe Cole a step debt; a pact secures his loyalty and reduces future betrayal risk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I propose a pact with Cole for mutual survival.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn wants me to align against Gus, but Gus saved me with the rope and has multiple jury debts. If I betray Gus, the jury sees it. If I side with Fenn against Gus, I might make finals but lose jury votes. Better to accept Gus's pact, keep options open, and not commit to Fenn's an

events.name: Cole
events.text: I accept Gus's offer. Solid moves matter.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus and I have a pact, but Cole is strong and may be the one to beat. I should solidify Cole while keeping Gus close. I'll accept Cole's offer to form a pact, then decide later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No public statement needed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have a pact with Fenn but breaking may gain trust with Cole; however waiting preserves options.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.name: Bex
Ash
Hana
Dara
Eli
Cole
events.text: I need to win jury votes. I betrayed Eli by voting him out despite our pact, but I kept pacts with Gus and Fenn. Hana saved me on the lever, Dara and Eli died by vote/trapdoor. I should emphasize loyalty to allies and frame hard choices as necessary survival, not malice.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I honored my pacts with Gus and Fenn to the end. Hard choices kept me alive; I never struck without need.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to make a plea that appeals to the jurors, especially Hana who saved me and Gus who saved me. Emphasize loyalty and decisive survival, but not softness.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I made hard calls, kept true pacts, and survived every trial. I'll value what this jury values: results and loyalty.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I must appear strong and self‑reliant while hinting that my pact with Cole secures the final challenge.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I will outlast and outplay, leveraging my pact with Cole for the win.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to ask a question that will reveal more about their alliances and betrayals. Cole's multiple pacts and betrayals make him a good target, as does Gus's broken pact with Eli. Fenn's seemingly shifting loyalties are also worth exploring.

events.name: Bex
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex asked silence—testing if I'll ramble and seem nervous. I should stay calm, concise, and remind jury I played strategically without unnecessary betrayal. Gus claimed he leveraged our pact; I need to reframe that I was the one driving our alliance, not being used.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Silence speaks, Bex. I made moves when needed, stayed loyal to those loyal to me, and I'm here.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I died on the bridge. I should ask Gus about his pact-breaking and voting me out, as that is a major betrayal.

events.name: Ash
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Gus
events.text: I must appear strategic, not betray any pact, while positioning myself as the optimal winner for the jury.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I navigated the hazards, kept my alliances where they served me, and now I’m the strongest contender for the prize.

events.name: Hana
events.text: All owe me lever debts; Cole honored final pacts without needless betrayal, Fenn stayed loyal to Gus who saved him, Gus betrayed Eli despite debt.

events.name: Hana
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana's silence is strategic—she wants me to fill the void and possibly overexplain or slip. I owe her a life debt from the lever, but she can't vote. The jury sees everything. I need to remind them I survived by skill, not luck, and honor debts where possible without groveling. G

events.name: Cole
events.text: I paid my debts, made my own calls, and earned my spot. Strength isn't noise—it's results.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole broke pacts with Gus and Eli and voted for me; Gus broke with Eli and voted him out, while saving me from the step. I want to test Fenn's loyalty and whether Gus's betrayal of Eli reveals his character, so I'll question Fenn.

events.name: Dara
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara's silence may be a test. I'll answer with poise, emphasizing my loyalty and survival without attacking rivals.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Silence asks what I value. I honor pacts, make hard calls, and earned my place through results and loyalty.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus broke our pact and voted me out despite his step debt. I'll force him to answer publicly; Cole held our pact to the end.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus, you broke our pact and voted me out. Why should anyone reward that betrayal?

events.name: Gus
events.text: I voted Eli out because he threatened my alliance with Cole; betrayal was strategic, not personal.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I acted to secure my position; eliminating Eli removed a threat to my alliances and my chance at the prize.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to craft a closing statement that secures jury votes. I have life debts to Hana and Gus, and pacts with Eli, Gus, Fenn. I broke none visibly. I paid debts, made strategic moves without overt betrayal. I should emphasize loyalty to those who mattered, results, and contrast

events.name: Cole
events.text: I kept every pact I made, paid every debt I owed, and eliminated no one who trusted me. Results without betrayal—that's my game.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to close strongly, reminding jurors of my integrity and the life debts I repaid, while subtly contrasting with Gus's betrayal of Eli.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I kept my word, saved lives, and made hard calls. Cole and Gus, you both made choices. I made mine with honor.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I must close now to lock in my final plea and avoid further jury questioning that could expose my betrayals.

events.name: Gus
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Gus
events.note: missing required public line; silence recorded

events.name: Bex
events.text: I must rank Cole, Fenn, and Gus. Cole has a debt to Hana for the lever and to Gus for the rope, but he broke pacts with Gus and Eli publicly. Fenn has a debt to Hana for the lever and to Gus for the step, and he formed pacts with Cole and Gus. Gus has a debt to Hana for the lever

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole kept his word and paid debts, showing integrity despite the chaotic alliances. Gus betrayed multiple pacts for personal gain, while Fenn was a loyal partner who made hard calls but ultimately fell short in strategy.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole honored pacts without betrayal, owes me lever debt, and claims clean game; Fenn loyal but followed betrayer Gus; Gus betrayed Eli despite debts and stayed silent.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole kept pacts and paid debts, and Fenn honored his word, while Gus broke pacts and voted out Eli and went silent at closing. Gus has the weakest record, so he ranks last. Cole's clean record edges Fenn for first place.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus broke our pact and voted me out, then gave no defense. Cole kept my pact; Fenn voted me but stayed loyal to Gus. Rank Cole first, Fenn second, Gus last.

events.name: Bex
events.reason: I must rank Cole, Fenn, and Gus.

events.name: Ash
events.reason: Cole kept his word and paid debts, showing integrity despite the chaotic alliances.

events.reason: Cole kept pacts and paid debts, and Fenn honored his word, while Gus broke pacts and voted out Eli and went silent at closing.

events.reason: Gus broke our pact and voted me out, then gave no defense.
